subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Builder's Brew
description: A 60-second lesson on The Builder's Brew.

hook.text: The 'builder's brew'—strong black tea with milk and sugar—is Britain's true national drink, not fancy Earl Grey.

buildup.text: It's brewed in a mug (not a cup), with the tea bag left in, stirred vigorously, and served milky and sweet.

discovery.text: This style emerged from factory tea breaks in the Industrial Revolution—fast, easy, and energizing for manual laborers.

twist.text: The 'milk first or last' debate has divided Britain for generations. Scientists say milk first produces a smoother cup.

climax.text: The builder's brew is class culture in a mug. It's unpretentious, democratic, and deeply embedded in British identity.

punchline.text: Strong, sweet, milky, fast. The real British cuppa isn't fancy—it's working.

quiz.question: Where did the builder's brew style originate?
options: Factory tea breaks during the Industrial Revolution
